provenance.notes: N is not a multiple of the column tile, so the last tile's out-of-range lanes must contribute nothing.
K is not a multiple of block_size, so the final block is partly out of range.
Rank-3 activation: the leading axes fold into the row count.
2-bit codes pack four per stored byte with a default zero point of 2.
8-bit codes are one byte per weight with a default zero point of 128.
A single-row decode with K=64 and block_size=32 exercises two independently scaled 32-element blocks per output column.
Expected values are independently derived from the ONNX Runtime schema. With normalization omitted, both projections read A directly.
Expected values are independently derived from the ONNX Runtime schema. SimplifiedLayerNormalization runs without projection biases.
Expected values are independently derived from the ONNX Runtime schema. SkipSimplifiedLayerNormalization uses both projection biases and returns the residual sum.

Five activation rows (M=5) with skip and norm_scale supplied but both projection biases omitted checks staged SkipSimplifiedLayerNormalization without the residual-sum output, at 4-bit block_size=16 quantization.
Ten activation rows over an eight-row tile dispatch two groups. The second group has two live rows and six guarded rows clamped to the last valid input.
Single row at K past two 128-code trips of the reduction-partitioned walk, with a partial final block and N not aligned to the decode column group.
Single row with an odd K, so the last reduction pair has one live code; skip input and residual output.

Inline-norm fused route (blob 8, so not the vector walk): the sum of squares accumulates across three 128-code trips of the pair walk, the odd K leaves one live code in the last pair, and N is not a whole column group.
Single row at 8 bits, where a code pair spans two stored slots, over two trips.
Single row without normalization, so the reduction-partitioned walk reads the raw activation.

K=64 at block 32 is two sixteen-byte vector groups per column, at most one per lane, so the decode walk covers eight columns per workgroup; N=13 leaves the second workgroup with a full first column group and a one-column second group, exercising the guards on columns 4..7.
Eight-column decode walk without the norm pass (plain activations, no skip): N=5 is one workgroup whose second column group holds a single live column.

K=2080 at block 32 is 65 sixteen-byte vector groups per column, more than the 64-lane decode workgroup, so the vector walk keeps both projections in every lane (no lane split) and lane 0 takes a second group; the staged norm covers 2080 activations.
